Title: Diagnosis of test `testContainsIgnoreCase_LocaleIndependence`

Details: The test `testContainsIgnoreCase_LocaleIndependence` verifies the behavior of `StringUtils.containsIgnoreCase` for different locales, especially focusing on locale-specific case transformations like Turkish 'i' and 'I' and some Greek letters. It ensures that the method correctly recognizes containment ignoring case differences under various default locales.

The code of `StringUtils.containsIgnoreCase(String str, String searchStr)` converts both strings to uppercase by calling `str.toUpperCase()` and `searchStr.toUpperCase()`, then uses `contains(strUppercase, searchStrUppercase)`. The `contains` method checks for containment by calling `str.indexOf(searchStr) >= 0`.

The fundamental problem is that `String.toUpperCase()` is locale-dependent and uses the default locale of the JVM unless supplied with an explicit locale. This means when the default locale is Turkish (or any other with locale-specific case rules), `.toUpperCase()` might produce unexpected results that cause false negatives or positives in string containment checks. The test sets the default locale to English, Turkish and back to default to detect this issue. 

Because the implementation relies on `String.toUpperCase()` without fixing the locale, the test fails when the locale is Turkish due to the distinct uppercase conversions (for instance 'i' to dotted or dotless I in Turkish).

The root cause is that `containsIgnoreCase` does not use a locale-independent method to do case-insensitive comparison, causing locale-dependent bugs.

Suggested methods to fix:
- `org.apache.commons.lang.StringUtils.containsIgnoreCase(java.lang.String, java.lang.String)`: Fix its usage of `toUpperCase()` by specifying `Locale.ROOT` or `Locale.ENGLISH` to avoid locale-dependent issues.

No other methods inspected appear directly involved in this bug.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
